haiku-low.q1: Sign-in works. The linked sub is matched and the Google email is ignored even if changed, then start_session runs.
haiku-low.q2: The user must submit the existing account's password on the confirm form. A correct password inserts the link row, then start_session runs.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5 the account locks for 15 minutes and the pending key is deleted, so the half-finished link is gone.
haiku-low.q4: Unlinked, verified, no email match: a user is created with no password and a link row, then a session starts. Unverified: login page message, nothing created.
haiku-low.q5: Outcome is an error page with nothing changed. After 12 minutes the state key has expired; a second load finds it already consumed by GETDEL.
haiku-low.q6: A normal start_session: a new sessions row and sid cookie, same as password login. An existing sid cookie's old sessions row is deleted first.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required; it needs a session and CSRF token. If that sub belongs to another user, Settings refuses and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: state, nonce and PKCE verifier sit in Redis key goauth:{state} with 600 s TTL. Atomic GETDEL at the first callback removes them, else TTL. Cookie g_attempt binds the browser.
haiku-low.q9: Redis key gconfirm:{token} holds sub, target user_id and next, TTL 600 s. Browser holds random token in cookie g_confirm. Success, lock or TTL deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In the user_google_accounts PostgreSQL table. sub is the primary key, so one Google account links to one user; user_id is UNIQUE, so one user has one Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user returns to the start page with: We could not complete sign-in with Google. Try again. The exchange is not retried, because the code is single-use.
haiku-low.q12: The Redis attempt record's mode is login or link. Link mode stores user_id; the callback requires the current session user to equal it, else an error page.

sonnet.q1: Nothing special. The Google email is ignored if the sub is already in user_google_accounts, even if it changed. They are signed in via start_session.
sonnet.q2: A pending link is created (Redis gconfirm:token with sub, user_id, next; cookie g_confirm) and a password form is shown. The user must submit the correct password via POST /login/google/confirm (g_confirm must match a live key, account not locked). On a right password, failed_logins resets, the key is claimed with DEL, the link row is inserted, and only then start_session runs.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins and shows the generic wrong-password message, and the pending key keeps its original TTL. On the fifth wrong password, locked_until is set to now + 15 minutes and failed_logins resets to 0. The gconfirm key is deleted and g_confirm cleared, so the half-finished link is gone. The user sees 'Account temporarily locked' on the login page.
sonnet.q4: If email_verified is true and no user matches, one transaction inserts a new user with no password and email_verified_at = now, plus the link row, and the user is signed in with start_session. If email_verified is false, nothing is created. The user goes to the login page with 'Your Google email isn't verified. Sign in with email and password.'
sonnet.q5: Both cases fail the same way. After 12 minutes the attempt has expired (TTL 10 min), so GETDEL finds no record. A second load finds the state already removed by the first callback. The outcome is an error page, and nothing changes.
sonnet.q6: It creates the normal session: the same sessions row and sid cookie as password login (no new session type), via start_session. If a sid cookie came in, start_session deletes the old sessions row, then inserts a new row, sets the new sid cookie, and redirects to next or /home.
sonnet.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required. Link mode only needs the session user to equal the attempt's user_id, and emails need not match. If the sub is linked to another user, or the user already has a different Google account, it is refused and the user returns to Account Settings with a short message. No state changes. If the sub is already linked to this same user, it goes back to Settings as done.
sonnet.q8: They are in Redis under goauth:{state}, with TTL 600 s. The browser is bound by cookie g_attempt = state. Redis removes them by atomic GETDEL at the first callback, otherwise by TTL expiry. The g_attempt cookie is cleared at the callback or expires.
sonnet.q9: It is held in Redis under gconfirm:{token}, containing sub, target user_id and next, with TTL 600 s from when the password form is first shown. The browser refers to it by cookie g_confirm = the random token. It is deleted on success (claimed with DEL), on account lock, or when the TTL expires. Wrong passwords do not extend it.
sonnet.q10: It is stored in the user_google_accounts table (sub, user_id, linked_at). sub is the PRIMARY KEY, so one Google account links to at most one user. user_id is NOT NULL UNIQUE with a foreign key to users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, so one user has at most one Google account. Unique-constraint violations from races are the final guard.
sonnet.q11: The user is returned to the start page (login page, or Account Settings in link mode). For a failed exchange or an invalid ID token the message is 'We could not complete sign-in with Google. Try again.' No state changes. There is no retry, because the code is single-use.
sonnet.q12: The attempt record in Redis stores the mode (login or link) and, for link mode, the user_id of the user who started it. In link mode the callback checks that the current session user equals the attempt's user_id. If there is no session or the user differs, it shows the error page. Starting a link also requires a session and a CSRF token.
